title: US Sets Nov. 10-11 Abu Dhabi Talks on Ukraine and Russia as Brussels Reconstruction Talks Continue
dek: Envoy Steve Witkoff said the US will mediate working-level negotiations in Abu Dhabi, while officials met at NATO headquarters in Brussels on postwar reconstruction and 2027 funding.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: Envoy Steve Witkoff wrote on X that "the United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on November 10-11 in Abu Dhabi," The Hill and Fox News reported.

Talks on postwar reconstruction, 2027 funding and security guarantees resumed Thursday at NATO headquarters in Brussels, AP reported, with the World Bank and BlackRock also attending, according to Ukraine's lead negotiator.
Zelensky said he held a 90-minute conversation late Wednesday with Witkoff and Jared Kushner, and that "the negotiations must move forward at full throttle," the AP reported.
The European Union sent Ukraine $4.9 billion for defense and public services, the AP reported.
body:
The United States will host working-level talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11, US envoy Steve Witkoff said, according to The Hill and Fox News. Witkoff posted the announcement on X. Axios also reported that the US, Russia and Ukraine would hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi on those dates.

## Brussels talks

In Brussels, Ukraine's lead negotiator Rustem Umerov said talks were continuing for a second day at NATO headquarters on postwar reconstruction, funding for 2027 and security guarantees backed by Ukraine's Western allies, the AP reported. Officials from the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, the European Union and NATO attended, along with the World Bank and the US investment group BlackRock, Umerov said.

Umerov wrote online that the group had "separately discussed the threats from Russia to Ukraine and all of Europe, as well as joint steps to counter them," according to the AP.

## Battlefield backdrop

The diplomacy comes as Russia and Ukraine exchanged airstrikes overnight. Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelensky said in a post on X that negotiations "must move forward at full throttle to bring this war to an end as quickly as possible." Meridian's overnight strike story covers those attacks.

## What is not yet known

The reporting reviewed for this story does not say whether the Abu Dhabi talks will produce any agreement, or what security guarantees either side would accept. Meridian will update this story if the talks are held, postponed or produce an announced result.

## What the talks cover

Umerov said the Brussels discussions focus on postwar reconstruction, funding for 2027 and security guarantees backed by Ukraine's Western allies. The AP reported that the meetings are taking place days before negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the United States are due to meet in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, for talks aimed at ending the war.

The Hill and Fox News reported that Witkoff framed the working-level negotiations as part of President Trump's mission to end the war. Axios reported that the three sides would hold peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11 in an effort to reach a breakthrough on a deal to end the war.

## Zelensky's account

Late Wednesday, Zelensky said he had held a 90-minute conversation with US negotiators Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the AP reported. In a post on X, Zelensky said that "Ukraine is ready to take the necessary steps" and that "our proposals are clear," according to the AP's account.

## Financial and humanitarian backdrop

The European Union sent Ukraine $4.9 billion for defense and public services, the AP reported. Russian strikes wounded civilians in the same period, while rescue teams searched rubble in southern Ukraine for missing people after a Russian strike that Zelensky said killed 43 people, according to the AP.
